subtype: Approach: rely on one person as the only support [Pitfall]
passage:
Vasudha, my roommate, was the only person I told. At first it felt like a relief, and I began to text her every time the low feeling came, then to talk at midnight, and by the second month at all hours. She listened, always, and I never asked her how she was.

Then she began wearing headphones in the room. She stayed late in the library. One evening she said quietly, "I care about you, but I can't be the only one you lean on. I'm running out." I felt as though a door had shut. Later I saw that I had put every low moment on one person, and that made us both feel worse. Ankita

qa.q: What did Vasudha begin wearing in the room?
qa.a: She began wearing headphones in the room.

qa.q: How did Ankita feel when Vasudha said she was running out?
qa.a: Ankita felt hurt and rejected, as though a door had shut, before realising later how much had been placed on Vasudha.

qa.q: What could Ankita have done earlier so support was not all on one person, and why?
qa.a: Ankita could have also talked to a counsellor or family, since one person alone cannot hold every difficult moment and may need rest.

qa.q: How does Vasudha experience Ankita's constant reaching out?
qa.a: Vasudha becomes tired and overwhelmed, hiding in headphones and the library, even though she cares.

grounding: A student relies on one roommate for every low moment, and the roommate becomes overwhelmed and withdraws.

subtype: Approach: rely on one person as the only support [Pitfall]
passage:
Warden's note, 3 March. Kishore, Block D.
This note is about two students in Room 214.
Since December, Divyansh has been going through a low patch. His roommate, Aman, became his only support: late-night talks most nights, walking him to class, answering texts during his own lectures. Divyansh told me he didn't want to 'bother' anyone else.
This week Aman came to me alone. He looked worn out. His own internals are next week, he hasn't slept properly in a month, and he has started staying in a friend's room to get some rest. 'I feel terrible, but I can't be everything,' he said.
Divyansh, meanwhile, feels abandoned and thinks Aman is angry with him.
I spoke to both separately today. Divyansh has agreed to see the counsellor this Thursday; I walked with him to book it, and he will call home this weekend. Aman is not to blame. I will meet both together next week.

qa.q: When has Divyansh agreed to see the counsellor?
How does Divyansh feel now that Aman is staying away?
qa.a: Abandoned, and worried that Aman is angry with him.

qa.q: What would make Divyansh's support sturdier?
qa.a: Adding the counsellor, calls home and perhaps another friend, so no single person carries every low moment.

qa.q: What is it like for Aman?
qa.a: Aman is worn out and guilty, caring about Divyansh but unable to be everything, especially with his own exams coming.

grounding: Shows a student leaning wholly on one roommate for every low moment until the roommate is overwhelmed and pulls back.

subtype: Approach: rely on one person as the only support [Pitfall]
passage:
Wednesday, 11 p.m. Vikas's diary.
Ganga moved her study table into the living room of our flat today. She said it's because of the light. I think it's because of me.
Since November she's been the one I call every time it gets dark in my head. 2 a.m., in the middle of her lab, the night before her interview. She always came. I never asked anyone else. My parents would worry, my college friends are busy, and Ganga just gets it.
Tonight I knocked and she said, 'Not tonight, Vikas, please.' She sounded so tired. I stood outside her door like an idiot.
I've been making her carry all of it. That's not fair to her, and it isn't even working for me, because now when she needs a break I've got nobody.
Tomorrow I'll go to the counselling centre and ask for an appointment. And I'll call Papa on Sunday, even if he worries.

qa.q: Where did Ganga move her study table?
qa.a: Into the living room of the flat.

qa.q: How did Vikas feel standing outside Ganga's door?
qa.a: Hurt and foolish at first, then guilty on realising how much Ganga had been carrying.

qa.q: Which other supports could Vikas add besides the counsellor and Papa?
qa.a: A college friend or a group activity, so there is more than one place to turn on dark days.

qa.q: What might Ganga be feeling when she says 'Not tonight'?
qa.a: Exhausted and probably guilty too, caring about Vikas but unable to keep carrying every low moment alone.

grounding: Shows a student relying on one flatmate for every low moment until the flatmate is drained and withdraws.
